description: The pie chart, titled “Answer Types,” visually represents the distribution of question formats within the MathOdyssey benchmark dataset, segmented into three categories: Open-Answer, True-False, and a third unlabeled category represented by a gray bar and labeled “(127)” in the legend. The largest segment, colored green, corresponds to Open-Answer questions, accounting for 63.0% of the total (244 items). The orange segment represents True-False questions, making up 32.8% (16 items). The smallest segment, colored blue, accounts for 4.1% and is labeled “True-False (16)” in the chart, though this appears to be a labeling inconsistency since the 16 items are already assigned to the orange True-False slice; the blue slice likely corresponds to the unlabeled gray bar labeled “(127)” in the legend, which may represent another question type not explicitly named in the pie chart. The chart includes percentage labels inside each slice and a legend on the left side identifying the categories and their counts. To the right, a box labeled “Examples” provides sample questions for each type: an Open-Answer problem involving prime numbers in a set, a Multi-Choice algebraic equation, and a True-False hypothesis testing question, illustrating the diversity of mathematical reasoning assessed by the benchmark.
